refinements.reason: Remove unintended paved spur continuing past the objective
refinements.prompt:
Edit only the supplied C — LONG DETOUR layout concept. Preserve the exact art style, continuous green landscape, orthographic camera, all object identities, the single red portal at upper right and the single blue soul objective at lower left.
There is a layout mistake: the road currently continues past the blue objective across the bottom and ends in a pointless spur at lower right. Remove that ENTIRE surplus bottom/lower-right road segment AFTER the objective and replace it seamlessly with the same meadow, grass/soil and sparse shrubs. Remove/relocate the towers and skeletons that were standing on that deleted spur, so none stands inexplicably on green ground.
The one retained gray route must be unambiguous: red portal at upper right -> across the broad upper arc toward the upper-left -> around the left-hand bend -> down the left side -> TERMINATE in a compact rounded gray arrival/building apron exactly under and around the blue objective at lower left. The objective is an ENDPOINT, not a roadside landmark. Keep a modest gray apron behind the objective only, not a road continuing across the bottom. Exactly one continuous gray band, exactly two ends occupied by the two landmarks, no forks, crossings, loops or extra dead ends.
Keep the big green central peninsula and open world beyond the paved band. Preserve some of the existing red-roof watchtowers and spoon catapults on the retained upper/left gray band, with free building space. No new architecture, obstacles, mechanics, arrows, UI or extra text. Preserve the existing small title C — LONG DETOUR. This is original concept art for human layout selection, not a measured map or gameplay screenshot.

variants.name: A — WIDE S
variants.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: original level-layout reference for the existing Not 3A Game, for human selection before implementation.
Input image 1 is the actual existing game's visual identity and object-scale reference, NOT its old map layout. Input image 2 is this project's original cartoon style board; use only its bottom gameplay strip as style guidance.
Create ONE polished wide landscape 16:9 elevated orthographic/isometric overview of a fantasy tower-defense battlefield embedded in a much larger continuous green world. Match the references' clean hand-painted cartoon treatment: short olive/yellow-green turf, warm earth pockets, worn cool-gray paving with grassy joints, sparse daisies, low shrubs and broken roadside masonry. Keep a single flat playable ground plane, daylight from upper left, fixed elevated tactical view without horizon. Grassland continues off ALL frame edges; no floating island, cliff boundary, perimeter wall or framed diorama.
Existing objects only: ONE intact dark slate circular portal with a vivid red vortex at the upper-right endpoint; ONE cyan soul sphere under a transparent ice dome on a slate bowl/base at the lower-left endpoint (the defended throne, NOT a castle or chair). Preserve their recognizable reference identities. Keep red-roof timber Rapid watchtowers, stone-enclosed wooden spoon catapults and a few small ragged cartoon skeletons at believable shared gameplay scale. All towers stand inside the gray buildable band, with some free gray building space remaining. A compact conifer cluster, pale granite boulders and dark rusty ore outcrops appear in the surrounding green land; no new resources or structures.
Primary layout requirement: replace the old broad straight diagonal paved area with ONE long, continuous, clearly winding gray invasion/building band from portal to objective. At consistent object scale the endpoint straight-line distance should be approximately twice the current game's baseline, whose portals are only about 8.6 cells apart; a first candidate targets about 17.2 cells direct separation. The winding travel path must be substantially longer than the direct segment. Show the full larger defense area by a pulled-back overview; concept camera zoom is only for seeing the layout. Keep portal and objective widely separated, not neighbors. The wider world is mostly green and open for later exploration; this is one battle district, not the whole final world.
Make the invasion zone a broad 5-6-tower-footprint-wide paved band with generous gray building pockets at a few bends, NOT a narrow one-character footpath and NOT the entire field painted gray. Opposite separated runs must have generous green gaps so they do not merge into shortcuts. No forks, intersections, dead ends, circular closed loops, bridges, gates or impassable decorative walls. A few skeletons distributed along the intended winding travel direction make its continuity readable, without a dotted line or arrows. Leave the route legible with restrained decoration.
Do not introduce factories, conveyors, automation, new tower types, UI panels, logos, a minimap, grid overlay, measurements or branded game references. This is a new illustrative layout concept, NOT a Unity screenshot or measured engineering drawing.
Variant A: a relaxed, organic S-shaped invasion band with TWO large alternating sweeps, broad almost-straight approach sections and soft but distinct corners. It should create three successive defense opportunities (portal approach, broad middle bend, final approach) while remaining easy to read. Do not make a tight serpentine, do not fold the two arms next to each other, do not make an omega/closed ring. Put only a small understated title "A — WIDE S" in the upper-left grass margin; otherwise no text. Favor believable landscape flow and useful unbuilt gray area over a decorative road.
